The One-Hundred Pillar Housc
LONG AN ~ 2004

INTRODUCHHON
A lIthough this is a neighboring province of
ồ Chí Minh City, the leading 1ndustrial
city nationwide, but until now Long An has been a
region bearing the bold characteristics of the Mekong
River delta with immense fields and abundant fruit-
trees and many kinds of attracting agricultural
specialties, with the West Vàm Cỏ and East Vàm Cỏ
rivers streaming over the provincial areas.
Especially on the Long An land nowadays one
could list hundreds of relics of all kinds, places
bearing the stamp of “labor, talent, intellect of the
consecutive generations... who have rushed into the
reclamation of this Vàm Cỏ river basin” exactly as
appraised: “Long An is beautiful but not very
beautiful, Long An is rich but less rich than the other
provinces. It is worthy to be cited that the moderate
richness and beauty of Long An today are the fruition
reaped of myriad hardships to overcome nature that
could be considered to be harsh” (Trần Văn Giàu:
Preface on The monograph of Long An Province -
=¬ Long An Publishers and Social Scientific Publishers,
1989). Moreover this land has been conferred the
title “Heroic Undaunted Land with all the people
fighting against the enemy” in the resistances full of
hardships and sacrifices In the past to save and defend
the country.

LỜI GIỚI THIỆÊU
MT dù là một địa phương giáp ranh với
Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh, thành phố công
nghiệp hàng đầu của cả nước, nhưng Long An cho
đến nay vẫn là vùng đất mang đậm nét đặc trưng
đồng bằng sông Cửu Long với ruộng đồng cây trái
mênh mông và nhiều loại đặc sản nông nghiệp hấp
dẫn, với sông nước Vàm Cỏ Tây và Vàm Cỏ Đông
chảy qua các vùng đất trong tính.
Đặc biệt, trên đất Long An hiện nay người ta
còn có thể liệt kê hàng trăm di tích các loại, nơi ghi
dấu ấn “công sức, tài năng, trí tuệ của các thế hệ nối
tiếp nhau... đổ vào khai phá vùng đất lưu vực sông
Vàm Cỏ này”, đúng như lời nhận xét: “Long An đẹp
mà không đẹp lắm. Long An giàu mà không giàu
bằng nhiều tỉnh khác. Điều đáng nêu là những cái
giàu, cái đẹp vừa phải của Long An ngày nay là kết
quả thu được của muôn trùng gian lao để khắc phục
một thiên nhiên có thể nói là vốn khá khắc nghiệt”
(Trần Văn Giàu : Lời tựa Địa chí Long An; NXB
- Long An & NXB Khoa học Xã hội; 1989). Và hơn
nữa, vùng đất này từng được phong tặng danh hiệu
“TRUNG DŨNG, KIÊN CƯỜNG, TOÀN DẦN
ĐÁNH GIẶC” trong những cuộc kháng chiến cứu
nước và giữ nước đầy gian khổ, hy sinh vừa qua...

For the above-mentioned sense, these booklets
In turn introduce the relics in Long An containing the
significance as the small works in the big collection
alming at preserving and bringing into play the
historical and cultural values of the locality in
particular and the Viet Nam country in general in a
PTOCeSS OỂ Opening for exchange relations and for
the integration into the region and the whole world in
all ñelds.
These booklets are written in a style of both
the mild literature and the strict documentary character
with the expectations to provide some basic and
necessary information for tourists who need to CaTry
out a fact-finding investigation at the country and
Long An people through every concrete relic.
We respectfully introduce it and look forwards
to receiving readers” opinions to enable the contents,
the forms of these booklets to be Improved more and
more in the future,
June 20”. 2004
Dr. HUỲNH QUỐC THẮNG
Rector of The College of Culture and Arts
in Hồ Chí Minh City

Với tỉnh thần đố, những tập sách mỏng lần lượt
giới thiệu về các di tích ở Long An mang ý nghĩa
như những công trình nhỏ trong một bộ sưu tập lớn
nhằm góp phần giữ gìn, phát huy các giá trị lịch sử —
văn hóa của địa phương nói riêng, của đất nước Việt
Nam nói chung trong quá trình sẵn sàng mở cửa để
giao lưu, hội nhập với khu vực và toàn thế giới trên
mọi lĩnh vực.
Những tập sách này được viết bằng một văn
phong vừa mang tính văn học nhẹ nhàng vừa có tính
tư liệu nghiêm túc với mong muốn cung cấp một số
thông tin cơ bản và cần thiết cho du khách có nhu. -
cầu tìm hiểu về đất nước, con người Long An thông
qua tìm hiểu từng di tích cụ thể.
Xin trân trọng giới thiệu và rất mong nhận được
các góp ý để nội dung, hình thức của những tập sách
này ngày càng hoàn thiện hơn.
Ngày 20 tháng Ó năm 2004
TS. HUỲNH QUỐC THẮNG

|9 knows that the southern Viet Nam in
general and the Mekong delta in particular is thc
biggest granary of the country. But for more concrete sight,
we see that this granary has developed according to the
time, to the big or small locality, to the export price of rice
in South-East Asian countries, and the increase in
population immigrating to the South. Due to the above-
mentioned backgrounds, we can understand why there is
the one-hundred pillar house made of precious timbers and
tiled roof while the Cần Đước area is relatively poor in
comparison with Cần Thơ, An Giang or Bạc Liêu (the
landlord's son in Bạc Liêu bought a sport plane under the
French domination).
The one-hundred pillar house in Cần Đước was built
from 1901 to 1903, at that time Cần Đước and Gò Công
Were the former land of the Southern Viet Nam Region.
We remember that the Lady Từ Dũ (King Tu Duc's mother)
was born at Gò Công. The people in the Central Viet Nam
iImmigrating to the South preferred Gò Công for many
reasons:
- . The Gò Công land was suitable to therice cultivation;
from the Central to Gò Công the access was near,
the transportation by boat was very quick, and they
didn't waste energy and time in comparison with
goïng to Sài Gòn. ñ
- Rice was the leading goods on the market of South-
East Asian Countries and this was our advantage.
- The rice of the alluvial soil had relatively high
productivity; the salty water made the rice quality
better; the price was the highest. We should know

They chose Long Hựu village, at that time according to the

Of the settlement, was a dignitary in the vililage headmasters

He reclaimed more than 500 ha of ground for rice
cultivation. He became very rich quickly since the price of
rice was high in the foreign countries and tenants liked to
gather there to work because the rice fields were good.

of 0.9 m high. The surface of its foundation was covered
with Chinese hexagonal tiles.
Looking at the plane plan one can feature the house
in the Sino-Vietnamese character “Quốc” (the country)
with three compartments and two lean-tos. It was exactly
the ancient style of tile-roofed houses with three
compartments and two lean-tos that could be seen scatterely
in the provinces of Southern Việt Nam and Sài Gòn. Some
years later, the main structure of 100 pillars has remained
the same but it was reinforced further in the perimeter to
120 pilHlars and then 160 ones. Later some around
compartments (the granary depository) were demolished.
The owner was the man who liked the carving.
Contemporarily he was nominated for “the dignitary in the
local Council” by the French administration.
The engraving looks too complicated, quite different
from the “present interior decoration ”. Formerly the house
Wwas divided into two parts:
- Thefront division was called the interior part, the
solemn place for worship of ancestors, sometimes
for precious guest reception.
- The back division was for the family :
accommodation and lifestyle.
Although the house has 100 pillars but we could
recognize that the owner had the sense of civic
responsibility so he did not want to decorate the house as
the great mandarins of the Nguyễn Dynasty did. The
ancestors” altar and the settecs were also simple. On this
point, I am astonished that it was quite different from the

landlords big occidental-styled houses in Cần Thơ and

landlords had ordercd the “ritual set” with two lines of

Concerning the structure of the one-hundred pillar
house in Long Hựu, we noted Nguyễn Tấn Quốc?s ï
documents compiled from the Long An Museum”s material:
; This is a structure of kingpost house; its frame is \
structured in eight pillars; it is located in the direction of
Western-South and front-back. The parts of the main
Structure such as rafters, girders are edged with seams and
bent-up-edged shape similar to the style of kingpost house
in the Central Việt Nam. The intersection between rafter
and girder supporting the ridge-beam is stylized in the shape
Of the pestle and the mortar which symbolize “the harmony
Of Ÿin and Yang (Therefore it is called the style of Mortar-
pestle house). This 1s the traditional house style which has
Very strong frame. The space in the middle of the house is
broad because it has not the centric row of pillars and it is
suitable for the worship of ancestors.
Especially the decoration of the one-hundred plllar 1
house features the carving art through the lay-out, the
©Xpression of the topic and the technique processing. The
whole system of rafters and obliques was carved in relief
and sunken carving meticulously such as the keenly specific
topics of “the cloud metamorphosing into Dragon”, “four
seasons stylized of leaf creepers”..

The researchers consider that the one-hundred plllar
house based on the engraving art of the Nguyen dynasty

30 The One-llundred Pillar House - Sơn Nam
THE ONE-HUNDRED PILLAR HOUSE
Cân Đước - Long An has been known not only about
the speciality of fragrant rice of Chợ Đào. but also about
many historical and cultural relics. If you have the
opportunity to come to Cần Đước, you should not drop by
an ancient architectural work at Long Hựu Đông village
which local people often call 7e One-Hundred Pillar House
(because this house has over 100 pillars).
Mr. Trần Văn Ngộ, the third generation owner, told
that this house was built in 1901 -1903 by his grandfather
Trần Văn Hoa, a village teacher at Long Hựu, Lộc Thành
Hạ canton, Chợ Lớn province. Its construction was carried
out by a group of workers from the Central Việt Nam.
With 1ts area of 882 square meter The One-Hundred
Pillar House 1s located on a garden of 4,044 square meter;
1ts facade 1s directed toward the North-West direction. The
house 1s completely of wood (dalbergia bariansis, sindora,
yellow sandal-tree...); its roof is covered with concave and
convex tiles; its 0.9m thick foundation is made of flagstone
and tiled of hexagonal rusúc bricks. Looking at the plane
plan one can feature the house in the Sino-Vietnamese
character “Quốc” (the country) consisting of three
compartments and two lean-tos. The house has two
divisions: The front division was called the interior part for
WOrship Of ancestors, sometimes for precious guest
reception; the back division was for the family
accommodation and hfestyle. The behind paddy storehouse
Wwas torn down in 1952, now the foundation has only
remained.

32 The One-Hundred Pillar House - Sơn Nam
The main structure of 7e One-Hundred Pillar House
¿s the kingposthouse; 1ts frame 1s structured in eight pillars;
1t is located in the direction of Western-South and front-
back. This 1s the traditional house style which has very
strong frame. Especially the decoration of fhe one-hundred
pillar house features the highly skilled carving art through
the lay-out, the expression of the topic and the technique
Drocessing on the system of rafters, netlike panels, pane
frames, parttions, altars, settees, round tables, rectangular
tables,.. by the very skillful and talented technique of inlay
carving, carving in relief, carving in relief on the inlay
background... The particular trait of this wood carving style
is beside the skillful and detailed realisúc style featuring
the transcription and affected by the feudal norms, it also
has the stylized and liberal style.
According to researchers, 7he One-Hundred Pillar
House was the style ofupdate house in the Nguyễn dynasty.
In general, it bore the stamp of Huế style but was performed
in the background of the South in the French domination;
therefore ithad many various minor details in the decoration
subjects creating the enrichment and the diversity which to
some extent expressed the history and the culture of the
South land in the late 19" century and the early 20" century.
Due to that value, The One-Hundred Pillar House was
classified the National historical and cultural relic by
Mimistry of Culture and Information in 1997 (Decision N° :
2890/VH-QĐ dated on 27 September 1997)
